idiom_name: Jakarta Bean Validation Validator.validate(obj, groups) invoked on demand
implementation_notes: Bean Validation is deferred by construction: constraints are declared on the class and evaluated when someone calls Validator.validate(obj, groups), so the gate lives in the operation that is about to use the object while Hibernate Validator supplies the ValidatorFactory and the constraint implementations. The returned Set<ConstraintViolation<T>> is the accumulator that replaces throwing from a setter, and validation groups with @GroupSequence size the check to the action - a Publish group that sequences the Draft rules plus cross-field rules. The classic hand-written validator tree is still the better fit when rules must be composed at runtime or loaded from configuration; for declared constraints the framework replaces it entirely.
pitfalls: Groups are not transitive: validating a Publish group does not run the Draft constraints unless the group is defined as a @GroupSequence including them, so a 'stricter' check can silently skip the cheaper rules.

The namespace split from javax.validation to jakarta.validation means constraints written for the old API are ignored by a new provider and the gate returns an empty violation set instead of an error.
ConstraintViolation instances hold references into the validated object, so keeping the violation set after the object is mutated makes the reported invalid values misleading.
